chunk_findings.detail:
The change still leaves `--json` producing **zero** JSON documents on the failure exits of two of the very commands it is meant to fix. In the function at line 127 (`reviewers detect`) the early-return path is unchanged:

```
if out.exit in (NOTHING, FAIL, REFUSED):
    print(out.reason, file=sys.stderr)
    return out.exit
c.out(out.data["text"], {"text": out.data["text"]})
```

so under `--json` the exit still writes only to stderr and nothing to stdout. The same pattern remains in `_reviewers_test`: when no reviewer matches (`if not targets` / name-not-found), it does `print(f"no reviewer named {a.name!r}; ...", file=sys.stderr); return FAIL` before reaching the new `c.out("\n".join(lines), {"reviewers": rows})`. Demonstration: in a repo with no reviewers, `ddflow reviewers detect --json` returns `NOTHING` with an empty stdout (previously "text"; now an empty stream), and `ddflow reviewers test --json --name nonexistent` returns `FAIL` with an empty stdout. The stated regression test is `tests/test_json_body_on_every_exit.py` with its skip list *removed* — i.e. it asserts a parseable JSON body "on every exit" — so these paths (empty stdout → `json.loads("")` raises) will still fail the un-skipped sweep, and the intent "each of those commands prints exactly one JSON document under `--json`" is not met. Every non-OK early return in these commands needs to emit the envelope (e.g. `c.out(out.reason, {"text": out.reason})`) before returning.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/review.py:127 (and :189)

chunk_findings.detail: When `c.json` is true, `_report_init` returns the structured `body` and never emits its text (`if quiet: return body` short-circuits before the `c.out(...)`). The adopt caller then prints only `c.out(out.data["text"], {**out.body(...), **(init or {})})`. In non-JSON mode the same command prints two texts to the user: `_report_init`'s report — `Initialised ddflow in <d> / config: <cfgp> / Next: ddflow phase add P1 --title 'First phase'` plus `commit_hint` and `rules_hint` — and then `out.data["text"]`. Under `--json` the report's prose is silently dropped: `root`, `config` and `rules_drift` survive as fields, but the next-step line, the commit hint ("what to commit", per the docstring) and the rules-drift advice ("…leaving your own prose alone.") have no corresponding field and are simply lost. So `ddflow adopt --json` in a repo with drifted rules produces a document whose text/fields differ from what `ddflow adopt` prints, contradicting the stated goal that each command put "the text in a field where it is the payload". The regression sweep in `tests/test_json_body_on_every_exit.py` only asserts stdout parses as a single JSON document, so it cannot catch this drop in content.

chunk_findings.detail:
The change only converts the *success* paths of `reviewers detect` and `reviewers test` to emit a JSON document. Both commands still have an early failure exit that writes only to stderr and returns without touching stdout:

- line 127 (`reviewers detect`): `if out.exit in (NOTHING, FAIL, REFUSED): print(out.reason, file=sys.stderr); return out.exit` — unchanged by the diff; only the following `print(out.data["text"])` was replaced with `c.out(out.data["text"], {"text": out.data["text"]})`.
- line 189 (`reviewers test`): `print(f"no reviewer named {a.name!r}; ...", file=sys.stderr); return FAIL` — also untouched; only the per-reviewer print loop was turned into `c.out("\n".join(lines), {"reviewers": rows})`.

Concrete failure: run `ddflow reviewers detect --json` in a repo where detection returns `NOTHING`/`FAIL`/`REFUSED`, or `ddflow reviewers test --json --name does-not-exist`. In both cases stdout stays empty (zero JSON documents), which is exactly what the de-skipped sweep test `tests/test_json_body_on_every_exit.py` rejects — so "the sweep passes with no skips" cannot hold for these exits. This is the same defect the earlier review reported (finding 1); the diff does not answer it because the early-return branches were left byte-for-byte identical, only the post-success print calls were changed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/review.py:127 (and ddflow/surfaces/commands/review.py:189)

chunk_findings.detail: The new parametrized regression test asserts only `json.loads(out)` and ignores the exit code. Because the CLI appends a fallback JSON body to stdout whenever nothing reached stdout (documented by the sibling test in this same file: "the fallback body is appended only when nothing reached stdout", and the pre-change assertion `'"refusal"' not in out`), any parametrization whose failure path writes only to stderr is satisfied by that fallback document, not by the command under test. Concretely, in a repo where only `ddflow init` has run: `("reviewers", "detect")` takes the `out.exit in (NOTHING, FAIL, REFUSED)` early return (nothing on stdout), and `("reviewers", "test", "nope")` takes the FAIL early return — the very paths the prior review quotes as unchanged (`print(out.reason, file=sys.stderr); return out.exit`). For both, stdout is empty, the fallback body is appended, `json.loads(out)` succeeds, and the case therefore passes before the fix as well as after it. These are precisely two of the commands the bug names, so the test provides no regression coverage for them and gives false assurance that they "print exactly one JSON document" of their own. To be a real regression test, each case needs to assert the payload (e.g. the command's message/exit field, distinguishing it from the generic refusal body), or the fallback must be made distinguishable.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_json_body_on_every_exit.py::test_text_commands_print_exactly_one_json_document

chunk_findings.detail: On the `out.exit in (NOTHING, FAIL, REFUSED)` path the function still only does `print(out.reason, file=sys.stderr)` and then `return out.exit` — it never calls `c.out(...)`. Under `--json` this leaves stdout completely empty, i.e. zero JSON documents rather than the "exactly one JSON document under --json" the change promises. The sweep test this change un-skips (`tests/test_json_body_on_every_exit.py`, which asserts a JSON body on *every* exit) will therefore fail for this command: e.g. running `ddflow reviewers test --json` in an environment where no reviewer resolves returns `NOTHING` with empty stdout, so parsing/validating the body fails. Note the asymmetry with `_reviewers_list`, which does emit `c.out(out.reason, {"reviewers": [], "message": out.reason})` on its own `NOTHING` path — the fix was applied there but not here, so the not-yet-removed skip for `reviewers test` is not actually safe to drop. The success path (`c.out(out.data["text"], {"text": out.data["text"]})`) is fine; it is only the error/empty exits that still produce no JSON body.

chunk_findings.detail: The change makes `_report_init` quiet-aware only at its *last* output: the new `if quiet: return {...}` guard sits after the `text = (...)` assignment, but the earlier `c.out(...)` call in the branch above it (the one ending "leaving your own prose alone.") is unchanged context and is still executed unconditionally. `adopt` now calls `_report_init(..., quiet=c.json)`, so under `--json` it expects this function to write nothing; when that branch's condition holds (its wording indicates an existing config/rules/prose file, i.e. re-adopting or adopting a tree that is already partly initialised), `_report_init` writes a plain-text document *and* `adopt` then writes its JSON envelope, so `ddflow adopt --json` again emits two documents on stdout and does not parse — exactly the bug this change claims to fix for `adopt`. The no-skip sweep regression will not catch this, because the sweep fixture is freshly created and never takes that branch. Fix: hoist the `quiet` check above every `c.out` in `_report_init` (or make `c.out` itself respect `quiet` for this call site) so no branch can print when `quiet=True`.

chunk_findings.detail: Both failure paths keep the pre-existing `print(<message>, file=sys.stderr)` and now additionally call `c.out(<same message>, …)`. Under the normal (non-`--json`) mode `c.out` prints its text argument to stdout — that is exactly why the other rewritten sites (`_reviewers_presets`, the `reviewers list` NOTHING branch, the reporting.py branch) could drop their `print`s and still emit the human-readable text. So a plain `ddflow reviewers detect` (no `--json`) that hits the `NOTHING/FAIL/REFUSED` branch, or a `ddflow reviewers test` with an unknown reviewer name, now emits the reason twice in one run: once on stderr and once on stdout. The change was scoped to `--json` output, so this new duplication on the human path is an unintended regression. Either the retained `file=sys.stderr` print should go (the `reviewers list` NOTHING branch shows the intended pattern: only `c.out` is used) or the stderr print is what the JSON branch should keep to itself.

The same file documents that the CLI appends a fallback JSON body to stdout whenever nothing reached stdout. Therefore, for any parametrization whose command takes a failure path, the assertion is satisfied by the fallback document rather than by the code under test. Concretely, if the `c.out(...)` calls just added at review.py:128 and review.py:190 were deleted again (i.e. the very bug being fixed), stdout would be empty on those runs, the CLI would append its fallback document, and this test would still pass. That means the regression test does not actually lock in the failure-path half of this fix and would not have failed on the unfixed code for those cases — contradicting the stated "watch it FAIL on the unfixed code" requirement and the hard constraint that the fix carry a regression test [D-rules-hierarchy]. Asserting the exit code (or asserting the refusal payload) for those parametrizations is needed to make the test meaningful.

chunk_findings.detail: `_report_init` now has a `quiet` flag, and the caller in the adopt path passes `quiet=c.json` so that the final report is folded into the single `c.out` document. But `quiet` guards **only** the final `c.out(text, body)`; the informational block earlier in the same function — the one that emits `"leaving your own prose alone."` — is left completely untouched. That block is a bare nested call with no `file=sys.stderr` (the same file uses `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` explicitly for stderr notes four lines above in the `hooks session-start` hunk), i.e. it is a `print(...)` to **stdout**. Given the input that makes the condition fire — adopting into a repo whose companion file (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/…) already contains user prose — `ddflow adopt --json` writes the `...leaving your own prose alone.` line to stdout and *then* the JSON document from `c.out`, so stdout is again not a single parseable JSON document. This is precisely the class of bug the change claims to fix, and the sweep regression test does not catch it because a fresh temp repo has no pre-existing prose, so the condition never fires. The fix needs to route this write through the same `quiet` flag (e.g. `if not quiet: print(...)`, or emit it to stderr).

chunk_findings.detail: Both failure paths keep the pre-existing `print(<message>, file=sys.stderr)` and now additionally call `c.out(<same message>, …)`. Under the normal (non-`--json`) mode `c.out` prints its text argument to stdout — that is exactly why the other rewritten sites (`_reviewers_presets`, the `reviewers list` NOTHING branch, the reporting.py branch) could drop their `print`s and still emit the human-readable text. So a plain `ddflow reviewers detect` (no `--json`) that hits the `NOTHING/FAIL/REFUSED` branch, or a `ddflow reviewers test` with an unknown reviewer name, now emits the reason twice in one run: once on stderr and once on stdout. The change was scoped to `--json` output, so this new duplication on the human path is an unintended regression. Either the retained `file=sys.stderr` print should go (the `reviewers list` NOTHING branch shows the intended pattern: only `c.out` is used) or the stderr print is what the JSON branch should keep to itself.

chunk_findings.detail: The prior finding still holds: the new parametrized regression test asserts only `json.loads(out)` and never checks the exit status. The same file documents that the CLI appends a fallback JSON body to stdout whenever nothing reached stdout. Therefore, for any parametrization whose command takes a failure path, the assertion is satisfied by the fallback document rather than by the code under test. Concretely, if the `c.out(...)` calls just added at review.py:128 and review.py:190 were deleted again (i.e. the very bug being fixed), stdout would be empty on those runs, the CLI would append its fallback document, and this test would still pass. That means the regression test does not actually lock in the failure-path half of this fix and would not have failed on the unfixed code for those cases — contradicting the stated "watch it FAIL on the unfixed code" requirement and the hard constraint that the fix carry a regression test [D-rules-hierarchy]. Asserting the exit code (or asserting the refusal payload) for those parametrizations is needed to make the test meaningful.

chunk_findings.detail: `_report_init` now has a `quiet` flag, and the caller in the adopt path passes `quiet=c.json` so that the final report is folded into the single `c.out` document. But `quiet` guards **only** the final `c.out(text, body)`; the informational block earlier in the same function — the one that emits `"leaving your own prose alone."` — is left completely untouched. That block is a bare nested call with no `file=sys.stderr` (the same file uses `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` explicitly for stderr notes four lines above in the `hooks session-start` hunk), i.e. it is a `print(...)` to **stdout**. Given the input that makes the condition fire — adopting into a repo whose companion file (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/…) already contains user prose — `ddflow adopt --json` writes the `...leaving your own prose alone.` line to stdout and *then* the JSON document from `c.out`, so stdout is again not a single parseable JSON document. This is precisely the class of bug the change claims to fix, and the sweep regression test does not catch it because a fresh temp repo has no pre-existing prose, so the condition never fires. The fix needs to route this write through the same `quiet` flag (e.g. `if not quiet: print(...)`, or emit it to stderr).
